name: Liberian Rice Bread
description: Rice bread, a dense, banana-and-rice-flour-based bread, is a genuine Liberian specialty distinct from wheat-based breads found elsewhere.
steps_detailed: Blend the cooked rice with the banana, sugar, and baking powder into a thick batter.
Bake at 350F (175C) for 30-35 minutes until set and golden.

name: Liberian Cassava Leaf Soup
description: Cassava leaf soup, pounded cassava leaves stewed with meat and real ground peanuts, is widely considered Liberia's national dish - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk in the peanut butter with a little water, then add the spinach.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until well combined.

name: Liberian Check Rice
description: Check rice, rice cooked together with greens and meat until well combined, is a genuine Liberian comfort food, similar in spirit to jollof but distinctly its own.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes.
Add the rice, tomatoes, and 1.25 cups water, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes.
Stir in the spinach in the last 5 minutes until wilted.

name: Liberian Palm Butter
description: Palm butter, meat stewed in real palm nut cream, is one of Liberia's most beloved dishes - real palm nut cream isn't a distinct item here, so peanut butter stands in for a similarly rich, reddish sauce.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, then add to the pot.
Simmer 25-28 minutes until the chicken is very tender.

name: Liberian Jollof Rice
description: Jollof rice, tomato-and-pepper rice cooked until it takes on real color and depth, is beloved across Liberia as it is throughout much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, and half the onion into a smooth puree.
Brown the chicken, 6-7 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the remaining onion, add the tomato paste, cook 2 minutes, then add the puree and simmer 15-18 minutes.
Stir in the rice and 1 cup water, add the chicken, cover, and simmer 20-25 minutes until tender.

name: Liberian Fufu
description: Fufu, cassava pounded into a smooth, stretchy dough, is a genuine Liberian staple, closely related to fufu found across much of West Africa.
steps_detailed: Boil the cassava until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Drain and pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy.
